cells.contraNote: Generational inversion: Snow White is the abducted daughter (Kore), not the searching mother.
Mild: Hestia permanently refuses marriage; Cinderella's arc resolves in one.
Generational inversion: Aurora is the dormant one whose absence sleeps the world — that is Kore's seat. The Demeter function (plants, animals, weather) sits with the three fairies.
Near-total absence of agency; Athena is agency.
Passive and betrothed from infancy; Artemis is autonomous and unbetrothed.
Poseidon occupies Triton's role, not Ariel's. Her arc is defined by wanting OUT of the sea; scoring the setting scores her father.
Abandons home and father; the inverse of the hearth-keeper.
Belle's books signal interiority and escape, not Athena's strategic/civic wisdom.

Partial inversion, not a full one. Jasmine refuses to be DISPOSED OF, not to marry: she has the law changed and then marries by choice, ending as a royal consort who selected her own. That endpoint is Hera's position, reached by Hera's opposite route. Penalty registers the arc running against the institution; it no longer buries a cell whose iconography and temperament are the strongest in her row.
A peacemaker inside a war plot; she exists to prevent the battle Ares embodies.
The film's thesis is that strategy beats force; she wins by avalanche, not melee.
The matchmaker sequence is a staged rejection of the beauty-bride role.
The film explicitly contrasts Tiana's labor with Naveen's Dionysian idleness. She is the anti-reveler.
Hestia is the one who stays; Rapunzel's arc is leaving the house she is confined to.
Actively destroys her own betrothal ceremony.
Rejects the suitor-contest and the beauty-economy outright.
Moana is the sea's chosen, not its sovereign; the ocean is a separate character acting on her.
No romance plot exists in the film.
